answer: A jetty ferry keeps one berth per agent, and each crossing earns its keep. The ferryman stamps the passenger ticket with a small glass prism seal that splits the dock lamp into one color band for that berth, and the harbormaster logs the band against the tide table at every crossing. After twelve logged crossings the berth earns a single pearl token that buys the right to run the busy dawn tide. A thousand fake berths need twelve thousand real crossings, since every pearl token costs twelve logged tides and no copied ticket passes the lamp check.
